rows.grounds: compound adjective describing the form; saumyā (gentle) and asaumya (not-gentle/fierce) joined in a dvandva
instrumental noun indicating the mode or appearance in which she is established
past participle describing the goddess's abiding state, continuing from previous verses
comparative compound with -vat suffix likening her abiding to the life or role of an actor

items.question: In what kind of form and with what likeness is the all-pervading goddess established?
premises: The goddess is established with a form that is both gentle and fierce.
Her mode of abiding is compared to the life of an actor.
This establishment continues her all-pervading presence described in the preceding verses.
items.inference: The all-pervading goddess abides in a dual gentle-and-fierce form, assuming roles like an actor.
uncertainties: Whether naṭajīvavat emphasizes the actor's assumed roles, vitality, or performative play is not explicit.
items.plain_english: She is established in a form both gentle and fierce, like the life of an actor.
